heading: Opposition to assistance for any government that fails to implement sanctions on North Korea

tree.heading: In general
tree.text: The Secretary of the Treasury shall instruct the United States Executive Director at each international financial institution (as defined in section 262r(c) of this title) that it is the policy of the United States to oppose the provision by that institution of financial assistance to a foreign government, other than assistance to support basic human needs, if the President determines that, in the year preceding consideration of approval of such assistance, the government has knowingly failed to adequately enforce sanctions under an applicable United Nations Security Council resolution (as defined in section 9202 of this title).

tree.heading: Waiver
tree.text: The President may waive subsection (a) for up to 180 days at a time with respect to a foreign government if the President—

children.text: the failure of the foreign government described in subsection (a) is due exclusively to a lack of capacity on the part of the foreign government;
the foreign government is taking effective steps to prevent recurrence of such failure; or
the waiver is in the national security interests of the United States; and
submits to Congress a report on the reasons for the determination under paragraph (1).

notes.heading: Repeal of Section
notes.text: Pub. L. 116–92, div. F, title LXXI, § 7124(b), Dec. 20, 2019, 133 Stat. 2249, provided that, effective on the date that is 10 years after Dec. 20, 2019, this section is repealed.

notes.heading: Codification
notes.text: Another section 73 of the Bretton Woods Agreements Act was enacted by Pub. L. 116–94 and is classified to section 286zz of this title.

notes.heading: Effective Date of Repeal
notes.text: Pub. L. 116–92, div. F, title LXXI, § 7124(b), Dec. 20, 2019, 133 Stat. 2249, provided that: “Effective on the date that is 10 years after the date of the enactment of this Act [Dec. 20, 2019], section 73 of the Bretton Woods Agreements Act [this section], as added by subsection (a), is repealed.”
